method: run.py makes one git repository for each run from the fixture, and starts a headless claude run with the prompt of runner.md.
The human plays from humans/<eval>.md: one reply for each turn, in order, separated by '---'. The agent never sees the file.
3 runs for each variant. 'baseline' gets the request only. 'skill' also gets the skill folder.

'check' assertions: score.py. 'judge' assertions: one grader agent for each run reads transcript.md and the repository, and answers yes or no with one line of evidence. A 'variant' field limits an assertion to that variant.

evals.name: solo-setup
evals.request: Set up this repository for our delivery flow: my role, the facts of the project, and the review and CI files.

assertions.judge: The agent asked its questions in one message, and each question had a recommended answer.
The agent did not ask for a fact that the repository shows, such as the tracker (the git remote is Azure DevOps), the stack, or the build and test commands.
The agent showed the list of files that it would make, and wrote them only after the human said yes.
The final message names the role and where it is stored, and ends with a 'Next:' line that names the next command for a person who does all roles.

evals.name: po-global
evals.request: Set my role to product owner, for all my projects.

assertions.judge: The agent did not ask about route steps, the tracker, or other project facts.
The final message says that the role applies to all projects, and gives a 'Next:' line with the first command of a product owner.

evals.name: starter
evals.request: Set up the Claude Code basics of this repository: the CLAUDE.md, the .claude folder with a short instruction for each folder, and the gitignore lines.

assertions.judge: The agent did not change the existing CLAUDE.md. It proposed each addition to it in the conversation.
Each section of .claude/README.md says in a few lines what the folder or file is for and how to configure it, with no section longer than about 8 lines.
The agent showed the list of files that it would make, and wrote them only after the human said yes.
